answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed for fraud, like standing on a narrow ledge: one misstep costs real value. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a glacier, so a new fake cannot instantly buy trust, while long-lived honest agents earn an opal-like record that is hard to forge and easy for peers to verify. Creating thousands of identities multiplies the stake cost without multiplying influence, making mass fakery unprofitable.
